HomeMax Retail - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

**Operator:**  
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the HomeMax Retail Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, instructions for queuing up will be given at that time. Please also note, today's event is being recorded.  

I would now like to turn the conference over to Jamie Patel, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

**Jamie Patel, VP of Investor Relations:**  
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and thank you for joining us today to discuss HomeMax Retail's results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on today’s call are David Morrison, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Wong, Chief Financial Officer; Tom Reilly, Chief Merchandising Officer; Karen Lopez, Chief Stores Officer; Mike Sullivan, Chief Marketing Officer; and Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer.  

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.  

With that, I’ll turn the call over to David Morrison.

**David Morrison, Chief Executive Officer:**  
Thank you, Jamie. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I’m pleased to report HomeMax Retail's performance for the Q3 2024. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities and delivered solid results despite the challenging macroeconomic environment.  

Today I will cover eight key aspects of our performance.  

First, overall performance. Our total net sales hit $2.85 billion, up 4.2% year-over-year, topping our guidance and showing three straight quarters of growth. Comps rose 3.8% on a 52-week basis, with traffic up 1.5% and average ticket at a five-year Q3 high of $145. Hardlines, 58% of sales, grew 5.1% on appliance demand, consumables up 7% on value pricing, while e-commerce at 18% of revenue grew 9%, prioritizing store fulfillment. Gross margins expanded 110 basis points to 32.4% from freight savings and mix, EBITDA $285 million up 12% at 10% margin, adjusted EPS $1.42 up 15%. Cash flow $320 million funded repurchases and a dividend increase to $0.25. Inventory down 8% to $2.1 billion at 10.2 weeks. Regionally, Sunbelt comps +4.5%, Northeast +2.1%. These results affirm our brick-first omnichannel approach, with stores driving 70% profits.  

Second, e-commerce growth. Omnichannel sales reached $1.2 billion, up 42% YoY and 28% of digital GMV, led by BOPIS at 2.8 million orders up 55% and curbside 1.9 million up 68%, boosting store traffic 12%.  

Third, store performance. Remodeled 185 stores to Essentials Hub format saw 9.2% comps versus chain 1.8%, traffic +6%, margins +120 bps.  

Fourth, marketing initiatives. Digital ROAS hit 6.2x, up 22%, driving 28% of store visits digitally influenced and $1.2 billion in digital-to-physical revenue.  

Fifth, supply chain optimization. Inventory turns 8.2x from 6.9x, $150 million savings, shrinkage down 22% to 1.1%, freight costs down 14%.  

Sixth, loyalty program update. HomeMax Rewards at 45 million members drove 22% of sales, 12% comp lift, with omnichannel members showing 35% higher repeats.  

Seventh, sustainability initiatives. Rail for 45% DC moves cut emissions 24%, 40% assortments ESG-certified, aligning with consumer preferences.  

Eighth, technology investments. AI demand sensing cut forecast error to 12%, RFID at 85% SKUs, automation in 12 DCs boosting picks 35%.  

We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.  

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Wong to provide more details on our financial results.

**Lisa Wong, Chief Financial Officer:**  
Thank you, David. Good morning. I'll provide a more detailed review of our financial performance for the Q3 2024.  

Our total revenue for the quarter was $2.85 billion, a 4.2% increase compared to the same period last year. Gross margin was 32.4%, primarily driven by reduced freight and logistics costs down 25% sequentially, favorable product mix shift to private labels, markdown discipline adding 200 basis points, and shrink improvement to 1.6%. Operating expenses were $620 million, representing 21.8% of revenue, benefiting from comp leverage and AI-optimized labor scheduling that cut overtime 15%. Net income was $210 million GAAP or adjusted $1.42 per share. We generated $320 million in cash flow from operations. Inventory levels are currently $2.1 billion, down 8% year-over-year and optimized at 10.2 weeks of supply.  

We are maintaining a strong balance sheet with $1.2 billion cash, net debt to EBITDA at 1.8x, and are well positioned to invest in our growth initiatives.  

Before turning to our other executives, let me share our financial outlook and guidance, including comp sales and earnings expectations. For Q4 2024, we guide consolidated net sales $2.85 billion to $2.95 billion, +3% to +6% YoY and flat to +3% comps, with U.S. comps +2% to +4%. Gross margin 38.2% to 38.7% up 50-100 bps from private label pricing and RFID shrinkage reductions. Adjusted operating income $285-310 million at 10-10.5% margin, SG&A 27.5-28%, EPS $0.85-$0.95 at 24.5% tax. For full FY25, sales $11.8-12.2 billion, +4-7% total and +3-5% comps, gross 38.5-39%, EBITDA $1.45-1.55 billion, FCF $900 million-$1 billion after $650 million capex. Comps for Q4 +2-4% with traffic +1-2%, ticket +1-2%, Sunbelt mid-single digits, Northeast flat to +1%, Canada +3-5%. FY25 comps +1-3% accelerating, driven by store refreshes, loyalty AI, home/garden +5-7%. This assumes 2.1% GDP, no recession, insulated by 55/45 essentials mix. Capex FY25 $650 million on remodels, AR app, just-walk-out pilots. Risks include CPI 3-4%, sentiment pullback, but upside from private label gains. Earnings guidance for next quarter thus EPS $0.85-0.95, FY25 implying mid-single EPS growth.  

Now, I'd like to hand it over to Tom Reilly, our Chief Merchandising Officer, to discuss our new product lines.

**Tom Reilly, Chief Merchandising Officer:**  
Thank you, Lisa. Good afternoon, everyone. As we wrap up our Q3 results, I want to dive deeper into our key strategic initiatives, which continue to drive meaningful progress across our 1,200-store brick-and-mortar footprint. Our physical network generates over 65% of total revenue, and we've advanced in store fleet optimization, omnichannel acceleration, supply chain resilience, and assortment innovation.  

On store fleet optimization, we're enhancing in-store experiences against experiential retail shifts. We remodeled 185 stores, up 25% YoY, to "Essentials Hub" format with demo zones for smart appliances and patio goods, like Best Buy labs. Remodeled comps +9.2% vs. chain +1.8%, traffic +6% from RFID planograms, margins +120 bps to 38.5% after rationalizing 15% low-velocity SKUs, markdowns down 22%. FY24 plans 250 more remodels in urban markets, closed 12 underperformers for $18 million gains. Sunbelt comps +4.5% in Texas/Florida from migration, Midwest -1.2% countered by micro-fulfillment in 15 pilots for 70% same-day within 10 miles.  

Omnichannel acceleration saw digital sales +28% to $450 million, 18% of revenue nearing Target's 20%, with BOPIS/curbside 55% of e-comm. Rewards at 28 million up 15%, Adobe personalization +22% repeats. App's Virtual Room Planner AR +14% furniture conversion, AWS microservices cut latency 40% for 5,000 TPM peaks, curbside under 2 minutes, comp lift +4%, omnichannel spend 2.5x pure e-comm.  

Supply chain resilience localized 40% imports to Mexico/Vietnam, lead times 45 to 28 days vs. Red Sea issues, SAP AI forecast 92% accuracy, turns 5.8x from 4.9x, stockouts -35%, new DCs in Atlanta/Phoenix/Chicago add 2 million sq ft for 1.2 billion units throughput, inventory -8% to $1.2 billion, EBITDA margins 7.2%.  

Assortment innovation pushed owned brands to 32% sales up from 25%, 15% higher margins like Costco, EcoEssentials sustainable bedding/furniture 35% sell-through per Nielsen millennial ESG demand 62%. Google Cloud dynamic pricing on 10,000 SKUs +50 bps margins vs. Wayfair, softlines vendor direct like Mohawk cut SG&A 3%.  

These position us for resilient growth in necessities +5% vs. durables -2% per Circana, FY24 comps 3-5%, digital +25%, capex $650 million, ROIC 12%. Risks 3.5% inflation, Amazon pressure, but density moat. Thank you.

**Karen Lopez, Chief Stores Officer:**  
Thank you, Tom. Good afternoon, everyone. We continue to focus on improving the customer experience in our stores, and omnichannel progress is a cornerstone of our transformation at HomeMax Retail. With 1,200 stores as our moat against e-commerce giants holding 38% online share per eMarketer, we're leveraging BOPIS and curbside for seamless experiences and high returns.  

Omnichannel sales hit $1.2 billion, +42% YoY, 28% digital GMV vs. 19% prior, ahead of 25% target, matching Target's 30%. BOPIS 2.8 million orders +55%, 22% online sales vs. 14%, AOV $145 +18% over $123 e-comm due to bundles avoiding shipping, 92% conversion, 2.1-hour hold via real-time sync. Curbside +68% to 1.9 million, 15% fulfillment, AOV $132 on decor/grills, 35% higher 30-day repeats. Northeast/Mid-Atlantic 32% penetration via geofencing 5-mile alerts like Starbucks, Southeast BOPIS +62% in Florida hurricane prep, Midwest rural 18% addressed by Indianapolis micro-DCs like Lowe's.  

$150 million in Omnichannel Orchestration Platform: RFID 85% SKUs paint/lumber/tools, latency <5 min, Oracle/Manhattan integration, 40% BOPIS ship-from-store, costs -22% to $4.50/order. App 14.2 million users +29%, AR +15% add-ons, Alexa voice pilot 28% conversion. Traffic +12% fulfillment days, 68% BOPIS add $28 in-store, 150 bps comp lift vs. NRF 2.1%, omnichannel margins +80 bps to 36.2% saving $8-12 shipping, SG&A 21% despite 7% picker wages via UKG. NPS 78 from 72, 84% cite convenience, 62% under-40 curbside GenZ/millennials, Pickup Perks +5% points, credit card 42%.  

Q4 30-32% digital GMV, BOPIS 25%, BOPIS+ lockers 600 stores like Best Buy, curbside grocery pilot 150, $200 million capex AI stockouts <5%. Risks macro sentiment, but essentials 45% resilient. Omnichannel 4x digital margins 14.2% vs. 3.5%, brick 85% sales. Excited for potential.

**Mike Sullivan, Chief Marketing Officer:**  
Thank you, Karen. Our digital marketing efforts have been highly effective this quarter, transforming from siloed ads to a flywheel boosting e-comm and store traffic across our 1,200 North America/Europe stores.  

Q3 digital spend $185 million +18%, 12% SG&A, ROAS 6.2x +22% from 5.1x, above 4.5x industry/eMarketer, Home Depot mid-5x, via CDP/Google/AppsFlyer 95% journeys. Google Search/Shopping 8.1x on $2B catalog, +25% near-me to 14% visits geo-fenced. Meta 5.8x DPAs +32% consideration HeroForge tools 35-54 demo. TikTok 7.2x GenZ decor, CTV 4.9x remodel awareness.  

28% of 145 million visits digital-influenced + from 22%, $1.2 billion revenue, 17% basket uplift app coupons 5-mile. BOPIS +41% 2.8 million 35% e-comm, 62% add in-store. CAC $28 -11% via CDP 1.5PB zero-party loyalty/WiFi, cookies -70%, LTV $1,240 +19% premium, repeats 4.2x.  

U.S. 72% budget 6.5x despite CPI 1.2% home goods, Sunbelt +35% traffic Amazon DSP vs. Lowe's. Canada 6.0x TikTok housing. Europe 5.7x GDPR, UK 42% Instagram click-collect vs. Argos, Germany +28% Otto, France owned email/SMS 42% open 8.1% CTR, APAC Australia 7.4x WeChat.  

Composable CDP Segment/Snowflake unifies 18 streams, Adobe AI churn 88% recover 22%, RMN $18 million 3x margins Sherwin-Williams, Chrome sandbox 85% Google. FY25 $250 million: zero-party quiz 10M users CAC -15% LTV +12%, QR AR Snapchat 20% uplift, Measured geo-tests 7x ROAS 35% traffic. CPMs +9-12% countered by 1,200 creative tests 3% fatigue, EDLP value vs. NRF 2.4% 2025 comps.  

Digital accelerates $2.3 billion revenue in $1.2T home sector, blending precision with store trust.

**Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer:**  
Thank you, Mike. We've heavily invested in technology advancements, particularly enhancing supply chain efficiency, which drove our outperformance with $150 million annualized savings, 220 bps gross margin to 28.4%, SG&A -15%.  

Inventory turns 8.2x from 6.9x highest peers, days 44 from 53, working capital -18% freeing $320 million, shrinkage 1.1% -22%, freight -14% $85 million vs. 25% industry spike, ocean 40% above pre-pandemic Drewry. $450 million NextGen roadmap across 28 DCs/1,200 stores.  

AI demand Oracle 95% SKUs 150k items, MAPE <12% from 28%, safety stock -25% stockouts 2%, back-to-school 94% accuracy vs. 82% vs. Walmart. GTP AutoStore 12 DCs +35% picks 450/hour 99.5% accuracy, Dallas mega-DC Honeywell robots -28% labor vs. $18/hour inflation. RFID 85% apparel WMS Manhattan -40% discrepancies, blockchain IBM groceries -30% recalls NielsenIQ 62% transparency. BOPIS <2 hours Exotec 400 stores +1.5 pts comps.  

U.S. nearshoring 35% apparel Mexico/Vietnam USMCA -22% freight 28-day leads post-LA congestion, throughput +18% 4% comps. Europe 22% sales UK/Germany 60% Turkey/EE -8 pts duties 15 days, Rotterdam automation vs. 12% wages, turns +11% flat comps vs. Macy's -2%. APAC 150 stores VMI P&G 40% Singapore +16% replen $12M, margins +180 bps 7.2%.  

SKU prune 15k <4x turns, private Essentials 28% sales 55% margins vs. 35% brands Costco-style. Rail Union Pacific 45% U.S. Scope 3 -24% freight -11% SEC/Deloitte 71%. Supplier scorecard 20% OTD 97% vs. CPI 3.2%/tariffs, 3 micro-DCs Atlanta/Chicago last-mile -19%. FY25 $200M savings turns 9x freight 3.8% COGS funds 7-9% comps 12-14% EPS vs. 5% unemployment.  

Supply chain is our weapon, double-digit ROIC, outpacing peers in omnichannel.  

Now, let's open the line for questions.

**Operator:**  
Thank you. Instructions for questions. Our first question comes from John Smith with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

**John Smith (JPMorgan):**  
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your sales?

**David Morrison:**  
Thanks, John. Inflation remains a headwind at 3-4% CPI on essentials, crimping discretionary like durables -2% per Circana, but our 55/45 essentials mix insulates, with value EDLP gaining share vs. discounters in $10-50 tier baskets +8%. Consumer sentiment mid-90s Conference Board, but housing starts 1.4 million tailwind hardlines +5.1%, private labels 42% mix shielding COGS volatility via scorecards.

**Operator:**  
Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

**Sarah Lee (Morgan Stanley):**  
What are your expectations for same-store sales growth in the next quarter?

**Lisa Wong:**  
Good question, Sarah. Q4 comps +2% to +4%, moderating from Q3 +3.8% but solid holiday, traffic +1-2% Black Friday events pop-ups 400 stores, ticket +1-2% decor +15% private apparel +12%. Conversion 28% BOPIS +25% top 200. Sunbelt mid-singles population/housing, Northeast/West +0-1% crime/office, Canada +3-5% CAD. FY25 +1-3% back-half scale, store RFID +50 bps/door, Rewards AI +8% visits, home/garden +5-7%, digital endless aisle +22%. No recession 2.1% GDP, inventory 3.2x weeks avoids markdowns.

**Operator:**  
Our next question comes from Mike Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

**David Morrison:**  
Thanks, Mike. Our supply chain improvements stem from $450 million NextGen, AI Oracle forecast <12% error safety -25%, AutoStore 12 DCs +35% picks, RFID 85% -40% errors, nearshoring 35% -22% freight. Turns 8.2x, savings $150M, regional U.S. +18% throughput, Europe localized -8 duties, APAC VMI +16%. SKU prune, rail -24% emissions, micro-DCs last-mile. FY25 $200M more, turns 9x.

**Operator:**  
Our next question comes from Lisa Green with Barclays. Please go ahead.

**David Morrison:**  
Hi Lisa. Loyalty via HomeMax Rewards 45 million up 14-18%, 22-25% sales, +12% comps households, personalization Adobe/Einstein +22% repeats, omnichannel 35% higher 30 days, Pickup Perks +5% points credit 42%, app 14.2M +29% AR +15% add-ons. Digitally acquired LTV $1,240 +19%, 4.2x repeats, win-back 22% churn recovery.

**Operator:**  
Our next question from Alex Rivera with Citi.

**Alex Rivera (Citi):**  
How are sustainability initiatives factoring into strategy?

**Tom Reilly:**  
Great point, Alex. Sustainability differentiates: rail 45% U.S. moves -24% Scope 3 -11% costs SEC-aligned Deloitte 71% preference, EcoEssentials recycled/FSC 35% sell-through millennials 62% ESG Nielsen, 40% assortments certified resonating 55% traffic.

**Operator:**  
Thank you. That concludes today's Q&A.

**David Morrison, Chief Executive Officer:**  
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our long-term strategy. Thank you for your continued support.

**Jamie Patel, VP of Investor Relations:**  
This concludes today's call. Thank you for joining us.
